'''Trevor Evans''' (26 April 1927 — 10 October 2010) was a British physical scientist who specialised in the properties of [[Diamond|diamonds]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=L. M.|last2=Mills|first2=I. M.|date=2021|title=Trevor Evans. 26 April 1927 — 10 October 2010|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2021.0033|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=72|pages=161–171 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2021.0033 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Evans grew up in Wales. Following national service in the [[Royal Air Force|RAF]], he moved to the [[University of Bristol]] to study [[physics]]. He later took up a research fellowship at the [[University of Reading]], where he would become head of the physics department and where his research career would be based. His work was supported by [[De Beers]], a firm for which Evans acted as a consultant.

He was elected fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] in 1962, and fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1988.<ref name=":0" />
